svg.text: XIAO ESP32-C5 (5.8 GHz receiver, C5VRX) to XIAO ESP32-S3 (Wi-Fi bridge). Seven wires: five video bits, the phone's receiver keys (on the bit 0 wire) and ground.
Wi-Fi bridge: camera port + JPEG + AP
receiver keys, S3 to C5 (UART; was video bit 0)
No other wires: the C5's back pads and S3 D8 stay free.
Video flows C5 → S3 (the C5's 6-bit DAC bus, 20 MS/s). The S3 inputs only listen: goggles on the DAC keep working.
Where the pins are: top view, USB-C at the top
Back side: leave all pads free
Back side: GPIO42 = MTMS pad, sample-clock loop
Optional: analog video for goggles (C5VRX's resistor DAC on the same pins)
• Power each board from its own USB-C cable; share only GND.
• Never join the two 5V pins while both are on USB.
• Keep the video wires short (< 5 cm); extra GND wires help.
• Antennas on both boards before power, kept apart.
• C5 D0–D3, D10 and the GPIO3–5 pads: never connect.
• S3 GPIO42 back pad: never connect (sample clock).
• Keys on D4: flash this repo's receiver build first,
then the S3 (the S3 drives D0 only while sending).
• Self-test (S3 console L) only with D0–D5 disconnected;
it refuses if it sees the C5 driving them.
ESP-VRX · tools/make_wiring_svg.py · C5VRX by Twotoz and the C5VRX contributors
